name: Harrison–Pemberton
description: Harrison West, Lillooet West and In-SHUCK-ch form the strongest documented southwest-BC through corridor.

name: Harrison East / Kookipi
description: Classic Harrison East–Shovel–Kookipi–Nahatlatch line; repairs, deactivation and recurring rockfall make through travel unreliable.

name: Hurley / Gold Bridge / Highline
description: High-country loop through Gold Bridge, Seton Portage and the exposed Highline; remote, steep and consequential.

name: Squamish River / Ashlu / Elaho
description: A major remote corridor in normal years, but the current Mud Creek and Ashlu bridge closures break through access.

name: Mamquam / Mount Mulligan
description: Approachable Squamish-area out-and-back with a rougher Ray Basin option; no legal continuation to Indian Arm.

name: Cheekye / Brohm Ridge
description: Steep, loose and water-barred riding ending at a legal vehicle gate near Brohm Ridge.

name: Callaghan Lake FSR
description: Short rough-gravel approach to Callaghan Lake with a legal annual motorized closure and possible late snow.

name: Lower Sunshine Coast network
description: B&K, Sechelt Roberts, Wilson and Dakota contain strong fragments, but a seamless Port Mellon loop is not proven.

name: Powell River Lakes
description: Promising northern Sunshine Coast loop with broad FSRs and rougher Rainbow Main; derived only as a road-intelligence lead.

name: Florence Lake / Stave West
description: Lower Mainland half-day out-and-back; the locked gate prevents the hoped-for Alouette connection.

name: Stave River / East Stave
description: Straightforward Stave out-and-back whose bridge/river condition prevents speculative cross-river continuity.

name: Chehalis Lake north beach
description: Approachable Harrison West–Mystery Creek ride to the old north Chehalis recreation area.

name: Big Silver Creek beaches
description: One of the Harrison area’s most approachable introduction rides, with current rockfall caution near km 13.

name: Lost Creek / Salisbury / Kenyon
description: Useful riding for about 10 km before sinkholes, deactivation and protected failed bridges.

name: American Creek
description: Modern out-and-back near Hope; the harder historical 30 km loop is not treated as current.

name: Liumchen East / Windy Knob
description: Water bars, ruts and steep loose grades; the emergency connector toward Cultus is not a public through route.

name: Tamihi motorized network
description: Stewarded green, blue and black technical riding area rather than a BDR-style travel route.

name: Foley Creek / Foley Lake
description: Easier road to Foley Lake, then narrow off-camber travel with drop-offs and 4×4-class terrain.

name: Nickelmine riding area
description: Established green through expert motorcycle network north of Hope; a riding destination, not a through route.

name: Vancouver Island Grand Loop
description: The clearest published Island-scale framework: 18 stages from Victoria to the north end and back.

name: Pacific Marine Circle
description: Reliable paved loop linking Victoria, Sooke, Port Renfrew, Lake Cowichan and Duncan; useful as the southern connector spine.

name: Port Renfrew–Lake Cowichan dirt
description: The easier VIGL dirt stage between Port Renfrew and Lake Cowichan, distinct from the paved coastal road.

name: Lake Cowichan–Bamfield
description: Moderate, remote westward resource-road crossing from Lake Cowichan to Bamfield.

name: Bamfield Main
description: Rebuilt and chip-sealed Bamfield–Port Alberni connector that remains an active industrial road.

name: Gold River–Woss
description: Signature north-Island crossing with potholes, washboard, loose stone and sparse services.

name: Woss–Port Alice via Atluck
description: The hardest main VIGL stage, with fist-sized gravel and remote cliff-side lake roads.

name: Alice Lake Loop
description: Signed karst-country loop near Port McNeill and Port Alice; vehicle access to Alice Lake itself is interrupted.

name: Port Alice–Cape Scott
description: Remote route through Coal Harbour and Holberg to the Cape Scott/San Josef vehicle trailhead.

name: Holberg–Port Hardy
description: North-Island dirt connector with deeper loose gravel and shared camper, shuttle and logging traffic.

name: Telegraph Cove–Sayward
description: Many branches and heavy logging make navigation more difficult than the riding itself.

name: Sayward–Campbell River backroads
description: Big Tree, Memekay and Morton Lake roads form a varied backroad stage with confusing junctions.

name: North Island 1000
description: The best concentrated Island BDR-style loop, joining remote north-Island communities with serious fuel and communication planning.

name: Khyber Pass alternate
description: Technical North Island 1000 alternate between Campbell River and Gold River; never a default big-bike route.

name: Tree to Sea Drive
description: Officially promoted all-vehicle Gold River–Tahsis route through dramatic mountain and lake country.

name: Great Canadian Roadbook Rally
description: Five navigation routes based near Sayward; useful as a route source, with access changing quickly during fire season.

name: Tansky ORV area
description: Approximately 1,000 hectares of signed south-Island motorcycle terrain from novice to hard enduro.

name: Whiskey Creek ORV area
description: Flowing central-Island singletrack with a kids’ track and steeper options; not a loaded ADV route.

name: Cook Creek riding area
description: Forested Bowser-area trail system mixing fast flow and hard-enduro terrain.

name: Tugwell–Alligator loop
description: Valuable historical Sooke route lead whose present gates, ownership and access have not been resolved.

name: Walker Lake / San Juan Ridge
description: Historic Shawnigan-area loop with an easier mainline and a washed-out advanced alternative.

name: Youbou–Port Alberni–Bamfield
description: Strong corridor concept, but modern gates, private land, bridges and road upgrades invalidate the old ready-to-ride GPX.

name: Shawnigan–Port Renfrew–Jordan River
description: Historical loop now broken by a removed bridge, a major washout and unresolved private/watershed access.

name: Tree to Sea research overlay
description: Useful current road-intelligence overlay, but not a motorcycle route because it includes bicycle-only and water-taxi connections.

name: Alberni Bam Bam research overlay
description: Road-research source containing trails, boat travel and private gates; not suitable for direct motorcycle use.

name: TCAT BC mainland
description: The canonical historic BC adventure backbone from Radium through the Interior and Coast Mountains to Horseshoe Bay.

name: TCAT Kootenay–Boundary
description: Radium–Kimberley–Purcells–Kootenay Lake–Kaslo–Trout Lake–Edgewood forms a standout multi-day interior section.

name: TCAT Chilcotin–Cariboo
description: Quesnel–Farwell Canyon–Gang Ranch–Big Bar–Lillooet–Anderson Lake–Pemberton through remote ranch country.

name: Gray Creek Pass
description: Iconic 2,072 m Kootenay crossing; latest notice scheduled repair completion but did not explicitly confirm through reopening.

name: Old Cascade Highway
description: Countless hairpins and no services on the Christina Lake–Rossland mountain crossing; distinct from the non-motorized Dewdney Trail.

name: Highway 31 / Trout Lake
description: Meadow Creek–Gerrard–Trout Lake connector; wide at first, then narrow one-lane road with hairpins and logging traffic.

name: Whipsaw Trail
description: Marquee Princeton-area technical overland route with slabs, boulders, mud and creek crossings.

name: Hurley River Road
description: Iconic Pemberton–Gold Bridge high pass with no services or cell coverage and rapidly changing washboard conditions.

name: Harrison–Pemberton TCAT link
description: Coastal link reused by Interior-scale itineraries; kept as a separate inventory record to preserve research provenance.

name: West Pavilion / Big Bar / Gang Ranch
description: Modular Fraser Canyon/Cariboo route with sustained climbs, ranch country, Farwell Canyon and the Big Bar reaction ferry.

name: Douglas Lake Road
description: Useful Westwold–Douglas Lake–Merritt connector whose older condition evidence needs modern fire, flood and gate validation.

name: Lac du Bois road circuit
description: Road-only circuit northwest of Kamloops; off-route motorized travel is prohibited in the protected area.

name: EVADRS Elk Valley bundle
description: The strongest local motorcycle-specific route collection around Fernie, Elk Valley and Koocanusa.

name: Koocanusa motorized network
description: Dorr-Grasmere, Caven, Linklater, Kikomun and Gold Creek form a major managed East Kootenay riding area.

name: Whiteswan / Lussier FSR
description: Scenic East Kootenay access road with a narrow canyon and active mining/logging traffic.

name: Top of the World access
description: Whiteswan-area gravel destination whose motorcycle-legal geometry ends at the park trailhead.

name: Settlers / Palliser / White River
description: Official road approaches to Height of the Rockies trailheads; the park trails are not motorized continuations.

name: Bull River–Hartley Pass–Fernie
description: Promising Galloway–Bull River–Sulphur Creek–Hartley Pass crossing whose exact motorized continuity still needs local verification.

name: Fernie–Flathead historic loop
description: The classic Flathead–Corbin–Cabin–Wigwam loop is no longer continuous because of washouts and removed bridges.

name: Elk River / Elk Lakes trailhead
description: Elkford–Cadorna Creek access road; Elk Lakes Park and the old powerline crossing are closed to motorized use.

name: Forestry Trunk Road
description: The closest long Canadian Rockies BDR analogue, running north from the Crowsnest area toward Grande Prairie.

name: Smith-Dorrien / Spray Lakes
description: High-value gravel road from Canmore through Spray Lakes toward lower Kananaskis; not the bike-only Great Divide line.

name: Mount 7 / Bowle-Evans
description: Compact, exposed Golden-area viewpoint road; more destination than cross-country connector.

name: Okanagan Falls OHV system
description: Official motorized trail system near the southern Okanagan; remain on designated routes.

name: Bear Creek OHV system
statusLabel: Map and pass rules need update
description: West Kelowna designated trail network whose published maps are old enough to require a current rules check.
